# Your money is yours. Right now, you can’t access it. Here’s what we’re doing.

*By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha*  
*Tuesday, 10 November 2026*

Since Friday, 6 November, you have not been able to withdraw your money from Pinha. Our payments partner, Northvale Payments, blocked all outgoing transfers at 09:00 that morning. Deposits and round-ups have also stopped.

**Your money has not been lost. It remains in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money, and Northvale cannot use it for its own purposes. But we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.**

That distinction matters. So does this: money you cannot access cannot pay your rent, cover a medical bill or help you through losing your job. Saying it is safeguarded does not make the situation acceptable.

I’m Inês. I’m a product designer at Pinha, and I write most of the words you see in the app. I’m writing this because you deserve a clear account of what happened, what we got wrong and what you can do now.

First, the most urgent part.

## If you need your money urgently

**Email urgent@pinha.example with the subject line URGENTE** if you need access to your savings for rent, medical costs or because you have lost your job.

We are trying to get Northvale to release funds individually in urgent cases. **We cannot guarantee that they will agree, or when a release might happen.** But please tell us if you are in this position so we can raise your case.

For other questions, our support team is still answering. We have received around 1,900 emails since Friday, and there are three people working through them. Replies are currently taking about two days. That is a long time to wait when the question is about your own money. I’m telling you so you know what to expect, not as an excuse.

**We have cancelled Pinha’s monthly fee for November and December for everyone.** You do not need to request this. It does not compensate for being locked out of your savings, but we will not charge you those fees.

## What happened

Northvale Payments is an e-money institution based in Vilnius. It is the partner that holds Pinha customers’ money.

On **Wednesday, 4 November**, Northvale emailed us a notice of “commercial termination”, giving us 30 days’ notice. The explanation was a “risk appetite review”. We have not been given a more specific reason.

Then, on **Friday, 6 November, at 09:00**, Northvale blocked all outgoing transfers without warning, before that notice period had ended and contrary to what the notice said. Deposits and round-ups also stopped.

We are angry about that decision. Northvale gave notice of one thing and then did another, leaving you unable to access money you had put aside.

On **Saturday, 7 November**, we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank.

Our CEO, Rui, is working with lawyers and speaking with Banco de Portugal. We are pursuing the release of your money and the steps needed to move to a new partner. Those conversations are necessary, but they are not the same as getting your withdrawals working again. That is the result we need.

## What “your money is safe” means here

I want to be precise, because a vague reassurance would be worse than useless.

Your money is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own funds. It is not money Northvale can use to run its business. It has not been lost.

The problem is access: Northvale has blocked outgoing transfers, and Pinha cannot move the funds until Northvale releases them.

So when we say your money is safe, we mean that it remains safeguarded. We do **not** mean that everything is fine, that you can withdraw it today or that we already have a confirmed date when you will be able to.

We know safeguarding is not enough when you need to use your savings now.

## We have signed a new partner. The move is not finished.

We have already signed with **Ostra Bank, based in Lisbon**, as our new payments partner.

That is a concrete step, but signing the agreement does not give us immediate access to the money Northvale holds. To complete the migration, we still need Northvale to send the balances file and Banco de Portugal to give its approval.

**Our current estimate for the migration is 10 to 15 working days. This is an estimate, not a confirmed withdrawal date.** It depends on steps we do not control, and it could take longer.

I know a firm date would be more useful. We do not have one we can honestly give you. We will not turn an estimate into a promise just to make this post easier to read.

## We got something important wrong

Northvale is responsible for its decision to block transfers. We are responsible for having built Pinha around a single payments partner, without a backup.

That was our mistake.

We trusted that arrangement to keep working, including during a notice period if the relationship ended. We did not have another route ready if our partner suddenly stopped transfers. You are now living with the consequences of that gap.

You did not choose Northvale. You chose Pinha. We cannot ask you to separate those things neatly when you open our app and cannot take out your savings.

I designed the screen that says: “Your money is always yours, take it out anytime.”

I look at that sentence now and feel sick. The money is still yours. But right now, the second half is not true. You relied on those words, and we are responsible for having put them there.

One user wrote to us after saving for three years towards a car deposit. The dealer is only holding it until this Friday, 13 November. That deadline is not going to move because we have a migration estimate.

There are people behind every support email, with plans and bills and decisions that cannot simply wait. We need to keep that in view in every call we make, not just in what we write here.

If you are angry with Northvale, I understand. I am too. If you are angry with us, that is fair. I’m not going to tell you to calm down or ask you to trust us because we have written a blog post.

We have to give you reasons to trust us through what happens next.

## What happens now

Our immediate priorities are to get funds released, pursue individual releases for urgent cases and complete the move to Ostra Bank.

For you, the practical points are:

- **If your situation is urgent:** email **urgent@pinha.example**, with **URGENTE** in the subject line. We are seeking individual releases, but cannot promise approval or timing.
- **If you have contacted support:** replies are currently taking about **two days**.
- **Your November and December monthly fees are cancelled**, with no request needed.
- **We will publish updates on this blog every Monday and Thursday until this is resolved.** The next update will be **Thursday, 12 November**.

Those updates will say what has changed, what is still blocked and whether the estimate has moved. If we are still waiting, we will say that rather than leave you guessing.

I’m sorry we put you in this position. You saved this money. You should be able to decide when to use it.

Our job now is to get that choice back to you.

Inês
